- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or volatile, model often underestimates; adjust upward, especially if recent price is falling.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior day), model frequently overshoots in next period; cap forecast at 1–2% below peak.
- If model forecast is significantly below true outcome (e.g., >5% gap), sentiment history suggests bullish reversal — increase forecast by 1–3%.
- If model forecast is significantly above true outcome (e.g., >5% gap), sentiment history suggests bearish correction — reduce forecast by 1–3%.
- Model tends to lag in mean reversion — if price is trending, forecast should be adjusted toward historical mean within 3–5 days.
- For 30-day horizon, model often underestimates late-period spikes (last 5–7 days); add 0.5–1.5% buffer if sentiment is bullish.
- If sentiment is mixed (±0.33–0.67), model is prone to oscillation — smooth forecast by averaging 3–5 prior values.
